races.name: Sticky Toffee Pudding Juvenile Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Vietnorm
runners_data.note: Best form in the field with back-to-back wins over 10f-16f on Good ground; Adrian Keatley's charge arrives 36 days fresh and looks the chief market danger to the favourite — naturally a hold-up horse on the flat but will need to race more prominently over hurdles here.|

runners_data.name: Wicksey
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with a recent win at 16f on Good; Ben Haslam sends this horse out as the key pace influence, and if allowed to stride on uncontested on a tight course like Cartmel the 63-day absence is the only meaningful query — style fit is flagged because the pace dynamics force it into a more prominent role than usual.|

runners_data.name: Jambearee
runners_data.note: A fader in the finish based on flagged pattern, and Brian Ellison's runner arrives on an 86-day break having shown little of note in recent flat form (finishing no better than fifth in five runs); though mapped to midfield, it is genuinely a hold-up horse shuffled forward by the field composition, meaning its chances in a front-runner's race are slim.|

runners_data.name: Lynxman
runners_data.note: Charlie Maggs (3lb claimer) partners a horse with zero wins or places on similar going in two attempts and a 130-day layoff; its true instinct is to race at the rear, not midfield as shown — a significant gap exists between its natural tactical position and where it will likely end up in this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Time Twister
runners_data.note: Jamie Hamilton rides for Michael & David Easterby and the yard has been busy (3/34 in 14 days), though this runner has failed to win or place on similar going in seven attempts; its natural preference is to come from off the pace, putting it at a structural disadvantage in a race Wicksey will likely run at its own tempo from start to finish.|

runners_data.name: Watcha Snoop
runners_data.note: Ryan Mania takes the ride on Adam Nicol's runner who has headgear listed (t=tongue tie) and arrives 30 days after last start; a fader in the finish with poor flat form, though one win and one place on similar going in nine attempts at least offers a small going angle — nevertheless, natural hold-up tendencies in a race with limited late opportunities make this a long-shot profile.|

runners_data.name: Royal Baroness
runners_data.note: Miss Becky Smith (7lb claimer) partners the lightest-weighted runner (145lbs) for R Mike Smith, who has been active recently (2/9 in 14 days); three placed efforts on soft or good-to-soft in five runs offers the most relevant going form in the field among the back markers, but being a true hold-up type mapped forward means it cannot naturally exploit that form without racing out of character.|

races.paceDynamic: Wicksey is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of seven and will control matters from the outset on Good To Soft ground at Cartmel's tight, turning track, setting a sustainable rather than pressurised gallop. With no genuine rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, Wicksey will dictate tempo from flag to finish, potentially stealing a march on a field that cannot organise a coherent pursuit. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate — Lynxman, Time Twister, Royal Baroness and Jambearee are all true off-the-pace horses shuffled forward on the map, meaning the genuine closers will be competing from further back than ideal, and none are likely to secure a prominent position naturally. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile — specifically a horse capable of racing close to Wicksey's steady pace and kicking on, rather than closers who must make up ground on a track that offers limited room to produce sustained late runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wicksey Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wicksey is allowed to bowl along on a solo lead and no rival applies early pressure through the race.
scenarios.body: Wicksey dictates a comfortable gallop around Cartmel's idiosyncratic circuit, preserving enough energy to assert from the final hurdle; the tight track and soft ground amplify the advantage of racing prominently. Vietnorm, who has the form and class to track the leader, is best placed to mount a challenge if Wicksey tires, but the unchallenged lead makes catching him very difficult.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Vietnorm Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Vietnorm settles smoothly in second and produces a well-timed challenge to overhaul Wicksey from the last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Vietnorm's flat form shows a natural hold-up tendency but OR=120 and strong recent bumper wins at 16f suggest this trip and conditions suit; ridden closer than usual by Oakley Brown, the five-pound claimer, the horse could exploit Wicksey's inevitable tiredness late on soft ground. Wicksey still sets the terms and gets first run, making it a tight battle, but Vietnorm's superior fitness at 36 days since last run gives it a credible chance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tired Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Wicksey fades sharply from two out having over-extended on soft ground and the hold-up horses find enough room to challenge.
scenarios.body: The tight Cartmel track and Good To Soft going could expose Wicksey's stamina limitations if the pace was slightly quicker than comfortable, opening a window for Vietnorm or Watcha Snoop to collide at the finish. However, the redistributed hold-up horses — Lynxman, Time Twister, Royal Baroness and Jambearee — are all racing out of role, reducing confidence that true staying-on closers are actually present to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Wicksey is pulled up, falls or the pace collapses entirely and the field concertinas into a messy bunched finish.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types falsely positioned in midfield, a pace collapse would cause significant interference and tactical confusion around Cartmel's narrow turns; no horse in the field is ideally suited to winning from a standing-still tactical crawl on this track. Watcha Snoop, who has headgear listed and a trainer angle to note, and Royal Baroness with soft-ground form could benefit from a scramble, though both carry limited confidence given their modest recent histories.

watchPoints.text: Wicksey's stamina at 2m1f over hurdles on Good To Soft after 63 days off is untested — if it weakens from two out, Vietnorm is poised to swoop and the race changes shape entirely.

With four genuine hold-up horses (Lynxman, Time Twister, Royal Baroness, Jambearee) all shuffled into midfield on the map but naturally wanting the rear, Cartmel's tight turns could produce traffic problems and interference in the closing stages — watch for stewards' enquiries.

Jambearee and Watcha Snoop are both flagged as horses that fade in the finish — if either is ridden prominently in error, they risk causing pace distortion before stopping, which could compromise runners around them.

Royal Baroness carries the lowest weight (145lbs) in the field with a 7lb claimer up — a combination worth monitoring if the race turns tactical, as a mistake or unseating from the amateur rider in testing conditions is a live possibility on a sharp jumping track.|

races.name: Campbell & Rowley Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Handmedownastar
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent recent form (five-run sequence includes two wins and two places) with a proven soft-ground record; Sean Bowen booking and Nick Scholfield's 2/14 trainer strike rate add confidence, though 99 days off is a minor query at 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Skipper
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who last won over 22f on Good but has struggled on Soft in the past (3/10 sim-going record); Shane Fenelon's 5lb claim could be useful, and connections (Mickey Bowen) are in form at 4/18 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: Veteran of 13 who favours soft ground (3 places from 15 runs) and goes with a hood; Nathan Moscrop takes over and the 44-day absence is standard, but his true profile is a hold-up horse who needs the pace to be honest enough to close into.

runners_data.name: Belvedere Blast
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer fitted with a tongue-tie and visor who has been running consistently in third/fourth territory on Good ground; the switch to soft over a longer trip could test stamina, and Oakley Brown's 5lb claim is noteworthy on a horse that has yet to win.

runners_data.name: Ballyearl
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner and therefore the key pace-maker; he won over 17f on Good but is unproven at 2m6f on soft, and his recent form (P8) suggests the step up in trip may not be straightforward for Danny McMenamin.

runners_data.name: Nottodaybobo
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent type who has won twice recently over 20f on Good going; soft ground is a slight query (9th and 3rd from 15 soft-ground runs) but the trip should suit and Micky Hammond's yard is firing at 4/10 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Rauzan
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse in terms of natural style, placed into midfield on the map because the rear is overcrowded — its chance depends on getting closer than usual to the pace, which the style-fit discount (0.90) reflects; best run on Soft was a 2nd over 20f, but consistency has been elusive.

runners_data.name: Secret Secret
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose jockey Brian Hughes is a major booking; ran just two days ago which is a significant freshness concern, and while his six-race form string is filled with places, he has not won since earlier in his career and the very quick turnaround must be flagged.

runners_data.name: Well Educated
runners_data.note: Three recent seconds on Good over shorter trips for this natural hold-up performer; the map places him in midfield rather than at the rear due to field congestion, and the style-fit discount (0.92) means his chance is best rated in a scenario where he can legitimately close from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Enya
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old prominent racer who ran well on Soft (1/5 sim-going) and has shown consistent placed form; Leah Noreci's 7lb claim is a boost in a handicap, but 113 days off and stepping from 16-17f to 2m6f are significant queries.

runners_data.name: Big Gypsy King
runners_data.note: Won over 17f on Good last time for the Moffatt yard; his natural style is hold-up but he's mapped to midfield given the congested rear — in a race with limited pace, a four-year-old needing to improve and find a new position will be tested, and the style-fit discount (0.92) is warranted.

runners_data.name: Dusky Days
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up finisher who has not shown winning form in recent outings (best of 067868); fitted with a visor and ran just two days ago like stablemates, and while he is placed in midfield on the map, his true role at the rear means he needs pace he is unlikely to get.

runners_data.name: Masterminding
runners_data.note: Has placed second and third in recent starts and carries the lowest OR in the field; naturally a hold-up horse shifted forward on the map due to field congestion, and Charlie Maggs' 3lb claim is a partial offset — the style-fit discount (0.91) tempers his claims unless a genuine pace materialises.

races.paceDynamic: Ballyearl is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival likely to press him from the outset, he should find himself in command at a tempo he can largely dictate across Cartmel's undulating 2m6f on Good to Soft ground. Handmedownastar and Secret Secret will push forward from their prominent positions, while Enya is also a natural mover-up, giving Ballyearl at least two or three horses for company in the early stages without being truly harassed. That controlled, sustainable gallop in soft ground over this extended trip is a classic setup that stretches the hold-up brigade — many of whom (Rauzan, Big Gypsy King, Well Educated, Dusky Days, Masterminding) have been pushed forward on the map precisely because the rear is overcrowded and they will not all find their natural berths. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track or press Ballyearl and produce a grinding late effort, with true hold-up closers disadvantaged by the lack of a truly fierce pace to chase.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ballyearl Controls, Prominence Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyearl leads at a measured clip and his prominent trackers outstay the hold-up horses in the soft ground finish.
scenarios.body: Ballyearl's uncontested lead allows him to conserve energy through the first half before stretching rivals from the front on Good to Soft Cartmel ground, and horses like Handmedownastar and Nottodaybobo — who have the form and fitness to sit just off the pace — can sweep past a fading leader without needing a strong early gallop to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Two Stay
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyearl sets a very modest pace and a prominent tracker such as Handmedownastar simply outstays him by travelling more smoothly throughout.
scenarios.body: The soft ground and extended trip punish a slow-burning front-runner who has failed to sparkle in recent starts, and a fit prominent type with strong soft-ground form can assert from the second-last flight without the race ever truly quickening.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Genuine, Late Closer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Ballyearl is pressured enough early that the race develops an honest tempo and one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to forge a genuine closing run.
scenarios.body: In this scenario a horse like Rauzan or Masterminding — both carrying style-fit discounts for being mapped out of their natural position — would need to overcome the handicap of racing closer than ideal and still find a meaningful late run on softish ground; this shape is plausible but structurally undermined by the redistribution crowding the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Test, Staying Form Tells
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground and the long Cartmel 2m6f trip produce a stamina-grinding test where early leaders fold and only the stoutest stayer prevails.
scenarios.body: Dinons, at 13 years old but a proven soft-ground stayer, and Fairlawn Skipper, who won last time over a staying trip on Good, could pick through tired rivals late in a battle of pure endurance; this scenario requires genuine pace and a taxing surface, and its probability is capped by the field's general lack of a strong pace-forcing presence.

watchPoints.text: Handmedownastar's last-time-out win combined with Sean Bowen riding and strong soft-going form makes him the key prominent threat if he travels smoothly just off Ballyearl — watch whether he gets an easy passage from his draw.

Ballyearl's recent form (P8) in uncontested lead races is a serious flag: if he capitulates turning for home having been allowed an easy lead, those tracking prominently will inherit the race, fundamentally changing which horses benefit.

Secret Secret ran only two days ago — monitor market moves and any late declarations; if connections are confident despite the quick turnaround and Brian Hughes commits, it is worth noting, but fitness risk on soft ground over 2m6f is real.

James Moffatt has four runners (Secret Secret, Big Gypsy King, Dusky Days, Masterminding) plus Enya and Well Educated — stable runners-to-winners ratio should be tracked closely as a yard this dominant in one race often has a single intended runner and the others as pacemakers or market anchors.

The soft-going record of hold-up horses in this field is poor across the board — Rauzan, Dinons, Belvedere Blast and Dusky Days all show thin sim-going returns — which reinforces that the race shape favouring prominent racers is not just a pace-map conclusion but is also supported by the going data.

races.name: EWGA Handicap Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Al Sayah
runners_data.note: A prominent racer whose recent form (4-4-1-3-4) includes a win over 24f on good ground and placed efforts on soft; Jack Tudor rides for Neil Mulholland (0/10 last 14 days, a concern), and similar-going form reads just 1W2P from 4 runs, but 45 days fresh and wearing a visor — well placed to press Kayf Dancer if the yard's form turns.

runners_data.name: Shallow River
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who needs things to fall right from off the pace; trainer Olly Murphy is in strong recent form (4/9 last 14 days), Sean Bowen takes over in the saddle, and the 10-year-old has won on soft over 25f — but soft-ground record reads 2W7P from 10 runs and a slowly-run race will blunt his late challenge significantly.

runners_data.name: Divilabother
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with an outstanding recent sequence (1-1-1-2-6) and three consecutive wins, all on good ground over distances between 20f and 24f — soft ground here is an unknown (0W3P in similar conditions per hist), but trainer Tristan Davidson hits 3/9 in the last fortnight and Harry Reed should ensure he travels comfortably in the first three.

runners_data.name: Imperial Merlin
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse returning from a lengthy 167-day absence, which is the longest layoff in the field; his best form comes on soft (1W3P from 9 similar-going runs, including a win over 24f) and the yard sends 3/16 over 14 days — his stamina profile suits the trip but fresh-horse queries and a slow pace conspire against him.

runners_data.name: Kayf Dancer
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, which gives him a precious tactical advantage in an uncontested lead scenario; 107 days off the track and just 0W2P on soft, with trainer Mickey Bowen firing at 4/18 over the fortnight — James Bowen takes a familiar booking and Kayf Dancer's last win came at 23f on good ground, making soft ground and the step to 25f his key questions.

runners_data.name: Imperial Data
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose recent form includes a fall and a pulled-up run (34-P8F), and whose redistribution to midfield reflects that there is no room at the rear for all the closers in this field — soft-ground experience is limited and Rebecca Menzies is 1/17 in the last 14 days; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) is a meaningful discount to his chance in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Belles Benefit
runners_data.note: Carries the lowest weight (149lbs) and showed a last-time-out win over 22f on good, but her natural closer's role is compromised by a field with too many genuine hold-up horses — Ben Case's stable sends 1/7 over 14 days, Harry Bannister rides, and the blinkered mare's best soft-ground effort is a sole placing from five attempts; the STYLE_FIT marker (0.93) reflects she is unlikely to get the late-race surge she needs.

races.paceDynamic: Kayf Dancer is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, is set to control this 3m1½f test at Cartmel on good-to-soft ground from the outset — dictating a steady, sustainable gallop that keeps the race well within his grasp for as long as possible. Behind him, Al Sayah and Divilabother will push to claim prominent positions, though neither has the natural gate-to-wire profile of Kayf Dancer, meaning the fractions are unlikely to be truly searching early. Shallow River and Imperial Merlin are legitimate hold-up types who will settle off the pace and rely on the race quickening late enough to allow their finishing efforts to count — a scenario made harder by the likely steady tempo set by an uncontested leader. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and horses close enough to the leader to pounce at the second-last, as the controlled pace will blunt the effect of any deep finishing kick from off the pace. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Imperial Data and Belles Benefit are genuine closers who are likely to find themselves racing closer to midfield than their natural position would suggest, and neither should be treated as a true backmarker beneficiary in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kayf Dancer Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kayf Dancer is allowed to bowl along in front at his own pace and the prominent horses cannot sustain a challenge from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Kayf Dancer sets a comfortable rhythm on good-to-soft Cartmel ground, with his rivals burning energy trying to close from two out while he conserves enough to hold on; Al Sayah and Divilabother, racing closest, are ideally placed to inherit if he weakens but may lack the finishing thrust to overhaul him.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Al Sayah or Divilabother applies enough sustained pressure from the home turn to wear down Kayf Dancer and take control at the last.
scenarios.body: The tempo, though steady early, accumulates over 3m1½f on soft ground and the prominent pair's stamina-laden profiles begin to tell on the run-in; Divilabother's recent winning streak at this trip and Al Sayah's course versatility make them the likeliest beneficiaries of a battle of attrition from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptively strong enough over the stiff Cartmel circuit to string out the field and open a late-finishing opportunity from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Shallow River and Imperial Merlin, both proven on soft ground with strong hold-up profiles, would need the race to fall apart in front to reach their target; Shallow River's trainer Olly Murphy is in sharp form (4/9 over 14 days) and Shallow River has won on soft, but a truly slow pace makes this scenario marginal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Scramble Home
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground takes a significant toll across the field and the race becomes a war of survival from three out with multiple horses stopping.
scenarios.body: Horses with strong soft-ground stamina and lower weight entries — Belles Benefit (149lbs) carrying least of all — could scramble home in a gruelling last-half mile as higher-rated rivals tire; however, both Belles Benefit and Imperial Data are redistributed hold-up types unlikely to be in the ideal position to capitalise, which limits this scenario's probability materially.

watchPoints.text: Kayf Dancer's ability to handle good-to-soft ground is a live concern — with just 0W2P on similar surfaces and 107 days off the track, any signs of him labouring from two out would open the race to Al Sayah and Divilabother immediately behind him.

Divilabother's three-race winning streak has been built entirely on good ground; if the Cartmel surface rides on the softer end of good-to-soft, watch for Harry Reed nursing him conservatively early to preserve stamina rather than pressing Kayf Dancer as expected.

Imperial Merlin's 167-day absence is the most significant freshness flag in the field — Sean Quinlan may need to produce an exceptional front-running performance from the hold-up position if he is ring-rusty, and watch for him being outpaced on the final bend.

Neil Mulholland's yard is 0/10 over the last 14 days — if Al Sayah shows any reluctance or flat-spots in running, a yard not in form could struggle to compensate through Jack Tudor's tactical adjustments.

Both Imperial Data and Belles Benefit are true closers likely to race in midfield rather than at the back — watch the early stages to see whether either settles naturally or burns energy trying to drop out against the traffic, which would further compromise their chances.

races.name: Wicks Group Cavendish Cup Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Grand Clermont
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a strong recent record including two wins from five in similar good ground; David Pipe's yard has a modest 14-day strike rate but this 10-year-old has proven course and distance credentials and Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim is a useful weight aid off 168lbs.

runners_data.name: Breizh River
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson's 8-year-old has won twice in five recent runs on good ground and handles the trip well; Harry Reed rides and the tongue-tie plus visor headgear combination suggests he needs some help to concentrate — a prominent position tracking the leader suits him ideally.

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's 6-year-old is the youngest in the field and has won twice recently, but all five historical runs have been on good or good-to-soft — the Good To Soft conditions here are not a concern and his 16-day turnaround with an active yard is a positive.

runners_data.name: Tommie Beau
runners_data.note: Jeff Mullins sends out this 11-year-old who is a natural front-runner by inclination, yet the crowded prominent tier means he is more likely to find himself in a midfield role that blunts his effectiveness; his best recent form over 29-30f suggests the trip suits but racing out of position is a material handicap.

runners_data.name: Caughtinyourtrance
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, recent back-to-back wins and a strong record tracking close confirm he is at peak form; Brian Hughes on a horse with tongue-tie and a hood who has won on good and good-to-soft ground — his control of the race from the front is the defining tactical factor.

runners_data.name: Stratagem
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's 10-year-old is naturally inclined to race prominently — two wins over 26-30f tell a story of a horse that needs to be on the pace — but the crowded front end pushes him back, and Mr James Murray's 7lb claim does not compensate for the style disadvantage this race shape creates.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Flyer
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride for his father's yard on this genuine hold-up performer whose three wins in five historical runs came when coming from off the pace; 55 days off is notable but the yard is in red-hot form (4/18 T14) and Fairlawn Flyer is the natural beneficiary if the front-end pace burns itself out.

races.paceDynamic: Caughtinyourtrance is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Brian Hughes aboard, will stride into the lead from the off over this 3m1½f Cartmel trip, setting a measured but honest gallop on Good To Soft ground that suits his profile — he has won twice in recent form and carries genuine front-running conviction. Grand Clermont, Breizh River, and Tamarind Bay are all prominent types who will look to track the leader in the first tier behind, creating a compact, well-strung-out shape rather than a chaotic early battle for position. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Tommie Beau and Stratagem are genuine prominent racers who are most likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield role they do not naturally seek, reducing their effectiveness. With a single uncontested pace-setter dictating a sustainable rhythm and several prominent chasers tracking close, this race shape strongly favours horses that can sit just off the leader, travel economically, and mount a sustained challenge from the second-last fence — the prominent-to-lead profile is the dominant beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Caughtinyourtrance Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Caughtinyourtrance bowls along in front at a controlled pace and the prominent chasers cannot peg him back from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Caughtinyourtrance dictates on his own terms across the full trip, the Good To Soft ground suiting his recent winning form, and his rivals burn energy chasing rather than saving for a late challenge; Hughes manages the fractions to perfection from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Reels Him In
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent tracking horses travels powerfully throughout and has enough in reserve to overhaul Caughtinyourtrance approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Grand Clermont or Breizh River, having sat a length or two off the pace, produces the stronger staying effort from the penultimate fence as the front-runner's advantage narrows; the key is that the chasing horse conserves energy early while Caughtinyourtrance does all the donkey work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Caughtinyourtrance sets a genuinely taxing early gallop on the testing ground and fades from the third-last, allowing a hold-up or midfield runner to come through.
scenarios.body: Fairlawn Flyer, operating naturally from off the pace, would be best positioned to pick up the pieces if the front end falls apart in the closing stages; Sean Bowen's experience gives the trainer's yard a strong chance of exploiting the late opening.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramblers Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If Tommie Beau or Stratagem manage to get closer to the pace than their redistributed map position suggests and produce a strong finish from an unexpected angle.
scenarios.body: Both are natural prominent racers forced into an unfamiliar role and would need the race to fall apart in front of them while also finding their natural rhythm mid-race — a low-probability double dependency; their STYLE_FIT discount means neither is ideally placed to exploit the shape they would need.

watchPoints.text: Caughtinyourtrance — if Brian Hughes is allowed to dictate unchallenged from the front, this horse is the primary threat; watch whether any prominent horse actively attempts to close the gap before the fourth-last or whether the leader is simply gifted the race from the front.

Tommie Beau and Stratagem — both will attempt to force their way to a prominent position despite the map suggesting midfield; if either succeeds in getting onto Caughtinyourtrance's quarters early, the pace dynamic changes materially and the front-runner's advantage is reduced.

Tamarind Bay — the 6-year-old is relatively unexposed over this trip (3m1½f is a step up) and James Bowen may find him running out of stamina in the closing stages if the early pace proves honest; watch him carefully jumping the cross-fence.

Fairlawn Flyer — Sean Bowen will be looking to produce this horse late and the Mickey Bowen yard's strike rate (4/18 in 14 days) suggests horses are in good order; if the race truly develops into a stamina test, his hold-up profile could make him a bigger player than his OR of 112 implies.

Grand Clermont — Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim means this horse carries a competitive weight off OR 132; his nine runs in similar going (2W 5P) is the strongest similar-going record in the field and is worth monitoring as a key angle in any scenario where the prominent profile prevails.

races.name: Fgh Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Pour Les Filles
runners_data.note: Consistent form at this trip on Good and Soft, tong-wearing prominent type who makes the running here without a rival to pressure her; the solo lead role suits her racing pattern but she has a tendency to finish in mid-pack in competitive fields, and the STYLE_FIT tag slightly moderates her winning prospects outright.

runners_data.name: Karnaval Point
runners_data.note: David Pipe's six-year-old has won twice at this sort of trip on good ground and brings a solid recent form figure; sits naturally prominent and with a 5lb claim from Rian Corcoran the weight advantage is material — textbook profile for the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: King Roly
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's hold-up horse returned to winning form 12 days ago and arrives fresh; goes well on Good but the soft ground is unproven over recent runs, and from a rear-tracking position at Cartmel's tight track he will need a clean run to deliver his challenge late.

runners_data.name: Bleu d'Enfer
runners_data.note: Donald McCain sends this eight-year-old without headgear change and a 50-day break; his best form shows ability to finish second from off the pace on Good ground, and while soft is fine for him, he has never reproduced that form on testing surfaces, making him a place candidate rather than a winner in the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Cossack Chach
runners_data.note: In truth a genuine hold-up horse most effective over shorter trips on Good, placed into midfield on the map because the rear is overpopulated; Lucinda Russell's six-year-old carries 71 days of freshness into this and a win over a shorter trip on Good last summer suggests the extra distance and soft ground are questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Sean Og
runners_data.note: Dianne Sayer's eight-year-old has won twice at 21f on Good and brings sound front-end form, but his natural style is to come from off the pace — positioned in midfield here because there are simply too many hold-up horses; soft ground is largely untested in his recent record, which is a concern at this level.

runners_data.name: Passengerontheship
runners_data.note: Sam England's horse carries a remarkable recent win sequence (five victories in last six starts) but those have largely come on Good ground; his true preference is to race from behind, and being nudged toward a midfield role in this map is not his natural comfort zone — his soft-ground record remains thin.

runners_data.name: Jack Sprat
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes partners this veteran who has placed at this sort of trip on Good, and his headgear (p) suggests he needs driving along; a true off-the-pace performer who is mapped to midfield simply through weight of numbers — carrying top weight at OR 99 on soft over 2m5f represents a stiff ask.

races.paceDynamic: Pour Les Filles is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop through the soft ground over 2m5f at Cartmel. Karnaval Point is the likeliest horse to press or sit just off the pace in the prominent berth, but behind those two the field is dominated by hold-up types — Cossack Chach, Sean Og, Passengerontheship, and Jack Sprat are all genuine off-the-pace horses who have been redistributed toward midfield on the map simply because the true rear is overcrowded. The field contains significantly more hold-up horses than the map can honestly place at the back, meaning Cossack Chach and Sean Og are most likely to actually secure a midfield pitch, while Passengerontheship and Jack Sprat may be forced further forward than they would like. With one horse controlling the pace and no pressure from behind, this race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who tracks Pour Les Filles at close range and has the stamina to sustain the effort through the closing stages — Karnaval Point's profile is the textbook beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Tracked Close
scenarios.trigger: If Pour Les Filles leads at a measured gallop and the prominent tracker lands upsides turning for home.
scenarios.body: Pour Les Filles sets a sedate pace that suits a horse sitting just off her shoulder, conserving energy for a two-out challenge on the soft ground; Karnaval Point, with a strong winning record at this sort of trip and going, is ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Pour Les Filles is simply allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the soft ground dulls the closers' finishing kicks.
scenarios.body: With no pace pressure she settles beautifully, builds a rhythm, and by the time midfield horses attempt to close the gap on the run-in the ground has sapped their momentum; horses with prominent or front-running tendencies who have settled well benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Get Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and the genuine hold-up horses find daylight to deliver their runs in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Bleu d'Enfer or King Roly, tucked in behind the midfield cluster, could emerge late if Pour Les Filles has emptied and Karnaval Point fails to pick up; however this scenario is tempered by the fact that several redistributed horses in midfield are not true hold-up types and may already be spent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Pour Les Filles weakens sharply at a fence and the field is suddenly leaderless with two miles covered.
scenarios.body: The absence of a natural second-string pace-setter means the race could momentarily stall before a prominent type asserts; any runner fresh enough to accelerate into the resulting gap benefits, but the soft ground punishes those who have chased hard throughout.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Karnaval Point can immediately slot in directly behind Pour Les Filles at the start — if he gets the prominent position cleanly, his form and jockey claim make him the most dangerous horse in the race.
Monitor Pour Les Filles at the first two fences; any jumping error under an uncontested lead could unsettle her rhythm and open the race up far earlier than expected.

Passengerontheship and Jack Sprat may be forced to race more prominently than their style allows if early positions are congested — horses out of their natural role in soft ground over this distance are vulnerable late.

Bleu d'Enfer has form to suggest he can stay on into minor positions from off the pace — watch whether Theo Gillard can find a clear passage down Cartmel's inside rail in the final circuit where gaps can close quickly.
King Roly's 12-day turnaround is notably short for a jumper; watch in the paddock for any signs of residual fatigue that could blunt what is otherwise a competitive profile for the closing stages.

races.name: Furness Rda Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Ghasham
runners_data.note: Consistent handicapper for Sam England who thrives on Good ground and has placed at this trip; genuine hold-up style suits a race that develops late, though soft-going record (0W3P on similar) tempers confidence; tongue tie fitted, 16 days fresh.|

runners_data.name: Achille Des Rocs
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and pace anchor — style fit of 0.92 flags he is racing out of his usual role somewhat, but as the only confirmed leader here his tactical position is ironically the most natural in the field; limited form on soft/heavy and light winning form in similar going warrants caution about his finishing effort.|

runners_data.name: Forcetoreckonwith
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes the ride for Greenall/Guerriero on a horse with an excellent soft-ground record (1W4P in five similar-going runs) and consistent form at this trip; returning after 130 days off is the key query, but the yard has been running horses into form and this horse tends to need the run less than most given its reliable placed profile.|

runners_data.name: Cuzco Du Mathan
runners_data.note: James Moffatt runner with an amateur jockey aboard and recent form figures of 644-78 that do not inspire; a natural hold-up horse pushed forward on the map because of field congestion at the rear — its true style means it will be further back than shown, making the task harder, and the weight of evidence points away from its chance here.|

runners_data.name: Wearelongterm
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with solid placed form over longer trips on soft ground (0W4P on similar), but has been running over 2m5f-3m and dropping back in trip here; a genuine hold-up type operating from midfield against its instincts, and the shorter distance on soft may catch it out when the race quickens.|

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes over on a 12-year-old who has been in tremendous nick lately (-23221), all form figures on Good ground — the complete absence of soft-going experience (0W0P on similar) is the standout concern; holds natural rear-of-field tendencies but has been racing prominently given recent good form, and Hughes is a positive booking.|

runners_data.name: Judicial Review
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is an obvious stamina and freshness question mark; holds a prominent racing style that suits this pace map naturally, and Callum Bewley retains the ride for Moffatt, but the quick turnaround over soft ground at this trip is a significant physical ask.|

runners_data.name: Blazing Court
runners_data.note: John Dixon trains and his amateur son rides — form figures of -UP720 are poor and include unseating and pulling up; a true hold-up horse shunted forward by the map's redistribution, meaning its real position will be at the rear where its form has consistently failed to deliver; significant concerns about competitive merit here.|

races.paceDynamic: Achille Des Rocs is the only confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, is set to bowl along at a controlled, self-imposed tempo over the 2m1½f trip on Good To Soft ground at Cartmel. Judicial Review will likely track from a prominent position, but the absence of any horse willing to seriously contest the lead means the pace will be honest rather than searching — a rhythm that suits a horse able to conserve energy and strike from the front or just off it. The pack behind Achille Des Rocs will be compressed, with Forcetoreckonwith and Ghasham the most natural hold-up types, but the field contains a heavy concentration of genuine hold-up horses — Cuzco Du Mathan, Wearelongterm, Getaway Jewel and Blazing Court are all true rear-of-field operators who are mapped to midfield only because there is no room for them all to sit out the back; the horses most likely to actually secure prominent positions behind Achille Des Rocs are Judicial Review and, if committed forward, Forcetoreckonwith. This race shape — a single uncontested leader, a compressed midfield, and genuine closers forced to race closer than they'd like — strongly favours a horse with the tactical speed to travel just off the controlled pace and outstay rivals in the closing stages rather than a true sit-and-sprint hold-up type.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Achille Sets Controlled Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Achille Des Rocs leads unchallenged and dictates a steady, sustainable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Achille Des Rocs bowls along in front without pressure, conserving energy on Good To Soft ground, and the race is set up for anything travelling comfortably just behind; Forcetoreckonwith, with strong soft-ground form and a record of finishing well from a tracking position, and Judicial Review, who should be prominent throughout, are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Find Room
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race, stringing the field out and creating the gap true closers need to finish through.
scenarios.body: The compressed midfield breaks up if Achille Des Rocs injects a burst on the final circuit, allowing genuine hold-up performers to thread past tiring rivals; Ghasham's consistent placed record and Getaway Jewel's recent run of form make them the most credible beneficiaries if late ground materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Leader Tires
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled tempo proves deceptively demanding on soft ground and Achille Des Rocs weakens turning for home.
scenarios.body: A slow-burning pace on soft turf can still take its toll on a front-runner who has been pulling from the front, opening the door for a horse with stamina reserves; Forcetoreckonwith's four placed efforts over this sort of terrain and Judicial Review's prominent position give them first claim on a spent leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field races in a tight, slowly-run cluster and the race turns into a sprint test from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A blanket finish favours the freshest legs and highest cruising speed rather than any tactical asset; Getaway Jewel's sharp recent form and Ghasham's consistency in competitive handicaps give them the best chance if the race is reduced to a rough-and-tumble dash.

watchPoints.text: Getaway Jewel has no recorded soft-ground form whatsoever — Brian Hughes is a strong booking but if the ground is the key variable, watch whether this horse handles the conditions as the early circuit unfolds.

Judicial Review ran just 48 hours ago; watch closely in the paddock and early stages for signs of fatigue or reluctance — a horse that fails to travel from the outset following a quick turnaround on soft ground could compromise the race shape if it fades from its prominent position.

Achille Des Rocs has a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 despite being the only front-runner — watch whether Danny McMenamin elects to push forward aggressively or instead drops the horse in, as any change in tactical intent could fundamentally alter the pace dynamic.

Forcetoreckonwith returns after 130 days off — watch the paddock for condition and the early jumps for jumping fluency, as a horse returning fresh after a long break on soft ground can take time to find its rhythm at the fences.
